prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1267; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured's driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. The responding officer recorded the claimant as present in the vehicle at the scene, and the report describes the impact as head-on at low speed.

Entry 3: Scene photographs and two independent witness statements were collected. Both witnesses describe the collision in the same sequence as the other driver's account.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as described and had no disagreement about the order of events.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The front-end damage pattern lines up with the reported impact, and the repair estimate reflects that same area and force.

Entry 6: Ran a prior-damage check on the vehicle and reviewed the file history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Attorney submitted the claimant's initial injury notice citing shoulder pain. The reported injury is consistent in type and severity with the force of a collision of this kind.

Entry 8: Requested prior medical records. No earlier injury to the same shoulder area is known from the records available so far.

Entry 9: Claimant gave a recorded statement through counsel. The account of the accident matches what was described in the first report.

Entry 10: Follow-up call with the claimant. The account given was the same as in every prior conversation, with no changes to the sequence or the details.

Entry 11: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of shoulder injury. Treating provider notes are being requested to document the reason for the extended course.

Entry 12: Reviewed the file. Coverage is confirmed for the named driver, the vehicle damage matches the described impact, and the claim will move to evaluation of the bodily injury portion pending the treating provider notes.
